# Objective

Make the worklog-selection-list plugin's chord shortcuts **extensible per project**: the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` provides the default chords, and a **project-local `shortcuts.json`** (discovered from the resolved worklog root) provides additional entries and overrides. Today `loadShortcutConfig()` reads only the bundled file, so projects cannot add project-specific chords without forking the plugin.

## Problem statement

A consuming project (open_source_llm) needs a `w` chord that dispatches `/skill:wiki-podcast-script --doc <path> --force-single` / `--rewrite <path>` to a pi agent pane for podcast episode work items. That chord is project-specific and must **not** be added to the core plugin's bundled `shortcuts.json` (operator decision). The plugin currently loads shortcuts exclusively from `join(__dirname, 'shortcuts.json')` (see `loadShortcutConfig()` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts`), so there is no supported way to add or override chords per project.

## Users

Herdr users of the worklog-selection-list plugin, and projects that consume it (e.g. open_source_llm's podcast production workflow).

- As a plugin user, I want the plugin's built-in chords (c, n, p, i, r, s, …) to remain available by default, so I can keep the standard workflow unchanged.
- As a project maintainer, I want to add project-specific chords (e.g. `w` → write podcast script) in a local file without editing the plugin source, so upgrades/rebuilds of the plugin do not lose my chords.
- As a project maintainer, I want a local chord with the same key sequence as a bundled one to override the bundled behavior, so I can tailor defaults per project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `loadShortcutConfig()` loads the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` as before (backward compatible; no local file → identical behavior to today).
- [ ] When a project-local `shortcuts.json` exists, its entries are merged: new chords are added, and a local entry whose chord sequence (+ view) matches a bundled entry overrides it (local wins). Override semantics are documented and unit-tested.
- [ ] The project-local file is resolved relative to the **worklog root** (the root that `configureWorklogTarget()` / `resolveWorklogRoot()` resolves from `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, i.e. the directory containing `.worklog/`), so the same plugin install serves different chords in different projects.
- [ ] Local file location and merge order are documented in the plugin README (config section), including the override rule and validation behavior.
- [ ] Malformed local entries are logged and skipped without breaking the bundled defaults (same defensive posture as the bundled parser; invalid values never crash or hide shortcuts).
- [ ] Existing chord behavior is unchanged when no local file is present; full `npm test` suite (shortcut-config tests and others) passes.

## Design notes / open questions

- **Local file location:** proposal is `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json` (next to `.worklog/`). Alternative: a hidden name (`.herdr/shortcuts.json` or `.pi/shortcuts.json`) to avoid a bare `shortcuts.json` in the project root. The worklog root already has `.worklog/`; a `shortcuts.json` next to it is simple and discoverable. Confirm which location is preferred (see Open Questions).
- **Override key:** chord sequence + view (`'list'|'detail'|'both'`) is the natural key. A local entry with the same chord+view replaces the bundled entry; same chord with a different view coexists. A local `stages` filter narrows availability (already supported by `ShortcutEntry`).
- **Merge mechanics:** `loadShortcutConfig()` currently takes no arguments. Extend it to accept the resolved worklog root (or read `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`), parse both files, and merge (bundled first, local appended/overriding). The registry already de-duplicates by exact lookup; explicit override handling must be added so duplicate chords do not produce ambiguous lookups (`lookupChordEntry` uses `entries.find` — the first match wins, so local entries must replace bundled ones at the same key, not just be appended).
- **`code_freeze`:** local entries may carry `code_freeze` like bundled ones (parser already supports it); no extra work expected.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `loadShortcutConfig()` merge logic, override handling, optional local-path argument.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — new tests: no-local-file (identical defaults), local adds new chord, local overrides bundled, malformed local entry skipped, per-project resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the resolved worklog root into `loadShortcutConfig()` (note: `loadShortcutConfig()` is currently called before `configureWorklogTarget()` in `main()`; the call order or plumbing must be adjusted so the local file is found).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the local `shortcuts.json` convention, merge/override rules, and location.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh` — no change expected (already passes `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`); confirm.

## Related work

- Consuming work item (open_source_llm worklog): **Add 'w' chord to write podcast script in ContextHub worklist plugin (OSL-0MSHFQ51L009IUOS)** — needs this extensibility to add its `w` chord without touching the plugin's bundled shortcuts.
- **Model selection per shortcut (WL-0MSD48ZFC0043AO3)** — added the `model` field to shortcut entries; the local-config extension must preserve it (parser already handles it).
- **Code-freeze shortcut visibility (WL-0MSD81VEL009XHWA)** — added `code_freeze` to shortcut entries; preserved by the same parser.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the project-local file should live at the worklog root (or a documented sub-path there) so the plugin can find it with the already-resolved root; exact name to be confirmed.
- **Risk:** duplicate chord sequences between bundled and local files must be resolved deterministically (local wins) or `entries.find` will silently pick the bundled one. Explicit override logic + tests mitigate.
- **Risk (scope creep):** full user-level config files (per-user, per-host), hot-reload of shortcuts, and UI for editing shortcuts are out of scope; track separately if requested.
- **Compatibility:** projects with no local file must see byte-for-byte identical behavior (guard against regressions).

## Open Questions

- **OPEN QUESTION (eng/producer):** Local file location — `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json` vs `<worklog-root>/.herdr/shortcuts.json` vs `<worklog-root>/.pi/shortcuts.json`? `.pi/settings.json` already exists at the project root of the consuming repo, so `.pi/` has precedent as a project-config location; `.herdr/` is more plugin-scoped. Recommend one and confirm.
- **OPEN QUESTION (eng):** Should the override key be chord+view only, or also stage? (Chord+view is the minimal key; stage is a visibility filter, not an identity.) Recommend chord+view.
data.title: Extensible shortcuts.json: bundled defaults + project-local overrides

# Write unit tests for auto-downgrade of critical priority

## Goal
Add comprehensive unit tests covering the auto-downgrade behavior for critical priority items transitioning to terminal states.

## Test Coverage Required

Per Acceptance Criteria 4 of parent (WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9):

1. **`wl update --status completed`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
2. **`wl update --stage in_review`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
3. **`wl close`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
4. **No-op: non-critical priorities** — verify high/medium/low unchanged on terminal transition
5. **No-op: non-terminal transitions** — verify critical priority unchanged when moving between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`)

## Implementation Notes

- Tests should use the existing test infrastructure (see `tests/database.test.ts` and `tests/cli/`)
- Follow the existing test patterns for `cascadePriorityDowngrade` tests
- Tests should verify both the priority change AND the reporting output (AC3 of parent)
- Consider both JSON and human-readable output paths

### Key Files
- `tests/database.test.ts` — database layer tests
- `tests/cli/` — CLI command tests (update, close)

# Intake Brief — Add a priority icon to the selection list (WL-0MTQYTA20009YXBT)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist selection list shows status, stage, producer review, and epic icons in its icon prefix, but the priority icon is only rendered as text after the title. Users scanning the list should see a priority icon alongside the other status indicators for at-a-glance prioritisation.

## Users

- **Primary**: Developers and operators using the Herdr worklist to browse and triage work items.
  - User story: "As a developer scanning the Herdr worklist, I want to see a priority icon as the first icon in each row so I can quickly identify urgent items without reading the full priority text."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Herdr worklist selection list icon prefix (in `getIconPrefix` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) includes a priority icon as the first icon, before the existing agent status slot.
2. The priority icon uses the existing `PRIORITY_ICONS` map from `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`: critical → 🚨, high → ⭐, medium → 📋, low → 🐢.
3. The priority icon respects the existing `noIcons` option — when icons are disabled, `PRIORITY_FALLBACK` text is shown instead.
4. The `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH` is increased to accommodate the additional icon (from 12 to 13 cells), and alignment is preserved.
5. The work item `priority` field is already passed through the item type accepted by `getIconPrefix`.
6. All existing tests continue to pass; new tests are added for the priority icon in the prefix (emoji, fallback, null/undefined priority, noIcons mode).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.

## Constraints

- Must extend the existing `getIconPrefix` function in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — do not create a parallel icon system.
- Must preserve the existing `WL_NO_ICONS=1` / `noIcons` option behaviour.
- Must not break the fixed-width alignment (`ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH`) — adjust the constant if needed.
- Visual-only change in the Herdr worklist rendering; no persisted data model changes.
- The priority icon must appear **first** in the icon prefix row.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`**: The `getIconPrefix` function composes an icon prefix with columns: agent status (fixed-width slot), status icon, stage/audit icon, producer review flag, and optional epic icon. The `PRIORITY_ICONS` and `PRIORITY_FALLBACK` maps exist but are not used in the prefix.
- **`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`**: Calls `getIconPrefix(item, { noIcons })` and prepends the result before the item ID/title. The `item` type already includes `priority?: string`.
- **Priority text** is already rendered after the title as `${priorityIcon(item.priority, { noIcons })} ${item.priority}` (line 1255 of worklist.ts).

## Desired change

1. **`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`**:
   - Update `getIconPrefix` to prepend the priority icon as the first icon in the prefix.
   - The new column layout (left to right):
     - 0. Priority icon
     - 1. Agent status (existing fixed-width slot)
     - 2. Status icon
     - 3. Stage icon (for in_review items, shows audit-aware icon instead)
     - 4. Producer review flag
     - 5. Optional epic icon
   - Update `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH` from 12 to 13 to account for the additional icon.
   - Update the JSDoc comment for `getIconPrefix` to document the new column layout.

2. **Tests**: Add/update tests for the priority icon in `getIconPrefix` (emoji, fallback, null/undefined priority, noIcons mode).

3. **Documentation**: Update any relevant documentation (e.g., `docs/icons-design.md` if it exists).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — Update `getIconPrefix` to prepend priority icon; update `ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — No changes needed (item type already includes `priority`)
- `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` — New tests for priority icon in `getIconPrefix`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icons.test.ts` — Updated tests verifying priority icon in rendered prefix

## Related work

- **WL-0MQEI5DYO009736I** — "Add stage and audit result icons to TUI work item selection list" (completed) — established the pattern for adding icons to `getIconPrefix`.
- **WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9** — "Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section" (completed) — ensured consistency between list and metadata sections.
- **packages/shared/src/icons.ts** — Core icon module; `PRIORITY_ICONS` map already defined.
- **packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts** — Worklist renderer that calls `getIconPrefix`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: Adding a priority icon increases the icon prefix width from 12 to 13 cells, which may reduce available width for the item ID/title on narrow terminals. Mitigation: The existing truncation logic in `worklist.ts` already handles width overflow — it truncates lines to fit the terminal.
- **Assumption**: The `item.priority` field is always available on items displayed in the worklist. If `item.priority` is undefined/null, the priority icon function returns an empty string (handled by the existing `PRIORITY_ICONS` lookup with a default empty string).
- **Assumption**: The priority icon emoji (🚨⭐📋🐢) are all single-cell wide in the terminal, matching other icons in the prefix.
- **Scope creep mitigation**: Any additional features (e.g., priority-based colouring of the entire row, priority sorting changes, priority filters in the metadata panel) should be recorded as separate linked work items rather than expanding this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Where should the priority icon appear in the icon prefix? The current order is: agent status, status icon, stage/audit icon, producer review flag, epic icon." — Answer: "The first icon in the row of icons in the selection list should be a priority icon." (from work item description). Final: priority icon is first in the prefix.
data.title: Add a priority icon to the selection list

# Child 1: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) runs `UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` (unless `--no-re-sort`), on create/update, so routine queue reads rewrite `updatedAt` on dozens of items at once (observed: 13 items at `2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z`, 88 items at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`).

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit. Concrete victim: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V audited "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03 now carries `updatedAt` 2026-09-11, so its passing audit reads stale and the item lingers in the open queue. Recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`) is also polluted.

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** a "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical re-sorts.
- **Heartbeat/audit pipeline:** must not re-audit items whose only change is sortIndex.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` (and the `database.ts:755-767` single-item re-sort path) no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- [ ] Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run `reSort`, assert the audit is still fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt` holds / freshness check passes) and `updatedAt` is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 behavior preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Check sibling: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` — `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:755-793` — re-sort paths; `:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`; `:2215` — recency scoring
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts`

## Related work

- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (freshness rule — preserve for semantic edits)
- WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (sibling timestamp symptom)
- WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF, WL-0MOYD0UAC003YJA3, WL-0MNX9XIQD005PUVW (auto re-sort features)
- Victim example: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V
data.title: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

# Improve pane auto-close logic (WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC)

## Problem statement

The current pane auto-close logic (controlled by `paneCloseEnabled`) is closing panes that should remain open. Since the default has been changed to `false`, the feature is currently inert — but when enabled, the classification logic needs improvement to avoid false-positive closes.

## Background

- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — "Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion" — established the pane-close scheduler and reaper infrastructure.
- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — "Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement" — created the pane-lifecycle classifier.
- The auto-close feature is now **disabled by default** (`paneCloseEnabled: false`) until the classification logic is improved.

## Current issues

The classification logic in `pane-lifecycle.ts` and `pane-close-reaper.ts` has been observed to close panes prematurely in certain scenarios:

1. **Intake panes** — May close before the operator has a chance to answer questions (when `needsProducerReview` is true but the state hasn't propagated).
2. **Plan panes** — May close before the producer has reviewed the output.
3. **Agent panes with long-running operations** — May be classified as idle when they are actually working but temporarily silent.
4. **Race conditions** — The pane-lifecycle monitor and the reaper may both attempt to close the same pane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No false-positive closes.** Pane auto-close must never close a pane where the operator might still need to interact (e.g. awaiting producer review, actively working, or has live child processes).
- **AC2 — Producer-review guard is robust.** A pane with `needsProducerReview=true` on its item must never be auto-closed, regardless of idle time or agent state.
- **AC3 — Active-agent detection is improved.** Pane-lifecycle classification must use additional signals beyond simple idle timeouts — e.g. recent file modifications, active network connections, or live child processes.
- **AC4 — Idempotent closes.** The reaper and the lifecycle monitor must not race; a pane can be closed at most once, with the outcome logged idempotently.
- **AC5 — Configurable grace period.** Add a `paneCloseGracePeriodMinutes` setting (default 5 minutes) — no pane is eligible for close within N minutes of its first dispatch, giving the agent time to start working.
- **AC6 — Better logging.** Every close decision includes a detailed reason with the full state snapshot (agent state, idle duration, item stage, needsProducerReview flag, child processes).
- **AC7 — Tests.** Table-driven tests for every classification path, including negative tests for the scenarios that previously caused false-positive closes.

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — Classification logic
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts` — Reaper orchestration
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.ts` — Scheduling and defaults
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Logging schema
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — Configuration options
data.title: Improve pane auto-close logic to avoid closing panes that need to stay open

# Add regression tests for false-positive pane closes

Parent: WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC — Improve pane auto-close logic to avoid closing panes that need to stay open.

## Context

The pane auto-close subsystem has never-close guards that should prevent false-positive closes, but they have not been pinned down with explicit regression tests for the scenarios that were observed to close panes prematurely. This child locks the current guard contract before the classifier is extended by sibling children.

## Scope

Write table-driven tests covering every existing classification path in `classifySession` (`packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts`) and the reaper orchestration (`packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts`), with explicit negative tests for the previously-observed false-positive scenarios. No production behaviour change in this child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1.1 (covers parent AC2 — Producer-review guard is robust): A pane with `needsProducerReview=true` on its item must never be auto-closed, regardless of idle time or agent state. For kinds intake, plan, audit and risk-effort the classifier returns `close: false` with reasonCode `producer-review`, even with an end-session marker present or a dead agent.
- AC1.2 (covers parent AC2): An `implement` pane is never auto-closed — `close: false` with reasonCode `implement` — even with an end-session marker and a dead agent.
- AC1.3 (covers parent AC1 — No false-positive closes): Pane auto-close must never close a pane where the operator might still need to interact — the invoking pane and any pane with `childProcessCount > 0` return `close: false` (`invoking-pane` / `live-children`).
- AC1.4 (covers parent AC1): A marker quoted mid-message or followed by non-whitespace must not close the pane (no false-positive marker detection).
- AC1.5 (covers parent AC4 — Idempotent closes): The reaper and the lifecycle monitor must not race; a pane can be closed at most once, with the outcome logged idempotently — running the reaper twice over the same still-live pane list closes it at most once.
- AC1.6 (covers parent AC7 — Tests): Table-driven tests for every classification path, including negative tests for the scenarios that previously caused false-positive closes; all run green against the current implementation.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts
- packages/herdr/src/pane-close.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts
- packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.test.ts
data.title: Add regression tests for false-positive pane closes

# Add configurable pane-close grace period

Parent: WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC — Improve pane auto-close logic to avoid closing panes that need to stay open.

## Context

No pane should be eligible for auto-close within N minutes of its first dispatch, giving the agent time to start working and producer-review state time to propagate. Today the reaper can close a pane as soon as its idle threshold is exceeded, with no minimum-age protection.

## Scope

Add a `paneCloseGracePeriodMinutes` setting (default 5), thread the pane's dispatch timestamp into reaper classification, and skip any pane still within its grace window. Covers parent AC5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC2.1 (covers parent AC5 — Configurable grace period): Add a `paneCloseGracePeriodMinutes` setting (default 5 minutes) — no pane is eligible for close within N minutes of its first dispatch, giving the agent time to start working; the value is clamped to [1, 1440] minutes and a non-finite value falls back to the default.
- AC2.2 (covers parent AC5): The reaper skips close for any pane whose age since first dispatch is <= the grace period, and closes normally once past it.
- AC2.3 (covers parent AC5): The scheduler reads the configured grace period from settings and passes it through to the reaper (settings in, skip out).
- AC2.4 (covers parent AC7 — Tests): Table-driven tests cover within grace, exactly at the boundary, past grace, absent/disabled grace, and a grace period longer than the idle threshold.
- AC2.5: All existing pane-close tests continue to pass.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.ts
- packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts
- packages/herdr/src/settings.ts
- packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.test.ts

# Improve active-agent detection signals

Parent: WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC — Improve pane auto-close logic to avoid closing panes that need to stay open.

## Context

The classifier currently treats an alive-but-idle agent as closeable via the `idle-threshold` path, which produces false positives when an agent is working but temporarily silent (long-running operations). Additional activity signals are needed.

## Scope

Extend the classifier with additional activity signals — recent file modifications and active network connections — and ensure live child processes keep the pane active. A pane showing any activity signal must never be closed by the idle-threshold path. Covers parent AC3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC3.1 (covers parent AC3 — Active-agent detection is improved): Pane-lifecycle classification must use additional signals beyond simple idle timeouts — e.g. recent file modifications, active network connections, or live child processes. `SessionSample` gains optional `hasRecentFileModifications` and `hasActiveNetworkConnections` with tolerant, defaulted handling.
- AC3.2 (covers parent AC3): `classifySession` returns `close: false` (reasonCode `active`) when an activity signal is set, even when `idleMs` exceeds the threshold.
- AC3.3 (covers parent AC3): The reaper passes the new signals from `PaneStatus` through `toSessionSample()`; absent signals default to no-activity (backwards compatible).
- AC3.4 (covers parent AC3): Never-close guards (implement, producer-review, invoking-pane, live-children) still take precedence over activity signals.
- AC3.5 (covers parent AC7 — Tests): Table-driven tests cover each signal independently and combined, plus the case where a signal is absent and the idle path still closes.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts
- packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts
- packages/herdr/src/pane-close.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.test.ts

# Bug — Audit immediately invalidated after completion

## Problem statement

When an audit passes, the herdr selection list immediately shows the work item as having an "out of date" (stale) audit. The root cause is that `currentFingerprint` is never computed or included in the `wl list` JSON output, so the fingerprint-based freshness check in `isAuditFresh` always falls back to the fragile 60-second timestamp gate. Any post-audit metadata change (comment, sync, assignee update) bumps `updatedAt`, making valid audits appear stale within seconds.

**Concrete example:** WL-0MUIB7D30009KG00 ("herdr stage filters hide in-progress items") completed a passed audit with `fingerprint: a0796548e6989b53cc51a824d3fa8aae7b0cc9eba255665dc043298eadf65b19`, but `currentFingerprint` is always `null` in `wl list` output. The herdr selection list therefore shows the audit as stale (bucket 5: "passed audit, stale") instead of fresh (bucket 6).

## Users

- **Herdr downtime worker (auto-dispatch):** Incorrectly re-dispatches audits for items that already have valid, content-unchanged audits.
- **Operators viewing the herdr selection list:** See "stale audit" indicators on recently-audited items, causing confusion and unnecessary audit re-runs.
- **Producers reviewing work items:** May see stale audit warnings that delay release decisions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`wl list` output includes `currentFingerprint`** — The `wl list --json` command computes and includes a `currentFingerprint` field for every work item in its output.
2. **`currentFingerprint` reflects description content** — The fingerprint is a SHA-256 hex digest of the item's description field (the same content used to generate audit fingerprints). The computation must be deterministic and consistent across runs.
3. **Herdr correctly shows fresh audits** — Items with a valid, content-unchanged audit show as "fresh" (bucket 6 in the in_review sort) in the herdr selection list, even if `updatedAt` was bumped by non-semantic changes after the audit.
4. **All project tests pass** — No regressions in existing tests; new tests cover the `currentFingerprint` computation and its effect on audit freshness.

## Constraints

- Change must be confined to the `wl list` command's output path (`src/commands/list.ts` and its helpers).
- The fingerprint must match the audit fingerprint format (SHA-256 hex string) to be compatible with the existing `isAuditFresh` fingerprint comparison.
- No schema changes required — `currentFingerprint` is computed at read time, not stored.

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh()` compares `fingerprint` vs `currentFingerprint` as the primary gate; falls back to 60-second time gate when either is missing.
- `src/commands/list.ts` — Outputs `fingerprint` from the stored audit result, but never computes `currentFingerprint`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `normalizeItem()` reads `currentFingerprint` from the raw JSON output (always `null`).
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `inReviewBucket()` calls `isAuditFresh()` with `currentFingerprint` (always `null`), causing the stale fallback.
- `src/audit.ts` — Audit fingerprints are extracted from audit text via `Audit content fingerprint: <sha256-hex>`. The description content is hashed by the AI agent during the audit run.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/list.ts` — Compute `currentFingerprint` and include it in the JSON output.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `computeCurrentFingerprint(description: string): string` helper (SHA-256 hex digest of description).
- `src/commands/list.test.ts` (or equivalent) — Tests for `currentFingerprint` computation and output.

## Risks & assumptions

1. **Fingerprint format mismatch** — The `currentFingerprint` must match the SHA-256 hex format used by audit fingerprints. If the AI agent hashes additional metadata (e.g., title, timestamps), the comparison will always fail. Assumption: the agent hashes only the description text.
2. **Performance** — Computing SHA-256 per item in `wl list` output is trivial for small repos but should be measured for large worklog databases. Risk is low.
3. **Scope creep** — Other commands (`wl show`, `wl next`) may also need `currentFingerprint`. Scope is `wl list` only; other commands are follow-ups.
4. **Backwards compatibility** — Adding `currentFingerprint` to the JSON output is additive and should not break consumers.

## Related work

- **WL-0MU1EWMHN000YUCG** — "Invalidating an audit" (smart re-instatement via `reconcileAuditInvalidation`; addresses the symptom by re-instating stale audits when content hasn't changed, but does not populate `currentFingerprint` for the primary freshness gate)
- **WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9** — "Audit freshness: keep audit valid after post-audit comments; persist auditedAt atomically; remove audit-content comments" (related freshness work)
- **WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K** — "Audit freshness: content-fingerprint gate as primary (port canonical fingerprint)" (introduced the fingerprint comparison gate that requires `currentFingerprint`)
- **WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS** — "Sync merges must not re-timestamp audit-fresh items (remove wall-clock updatedAt bump)" (timestamp churn issue)
- **WL-0MUNZHJIZ002IWBO** — "[test-failure] npm --silent test -- tests/cli — failing test" (failing test that was inherited from the parent audit of WL-0MUIB7D30009KG00)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions required — the root cause is clear from code inspection.

# Child 2: Fix same-timestamp merge from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO (Invalidating an audit).

## Problem statement

`mergeSameTimestampItems` in `packages/shared/src/sync.ts:~L423` sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content. This causes an unbounded timestamp advancement on repeated syncs, invalidating previously-passing audits.

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit, causing passing audits to read as stale.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl sync`:** Sync should converge without advancing timestamps unboundedly.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited but invalidated only by timestamp churn from sync.
- **Producers:** An audited item must retain its audit freshness across sync operations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mergeSameTimestampItems` only bumps `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field; converges without bumping when the merged result equals one side.
- [ ] Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` synced repeatedly converge with no unbounded timestamp advancement; existing audit freshness preserved.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing behaviour preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Preserve existing merge semantics for content resolution; only skip the timestamp bump when the merged result equals one side.
- Check sibling: WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA (re-sort updatedAt churn) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts:~L423` — `mergeSameTimestampItems`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`

## Related work

- WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO (parent: Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations)
- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (freshness rule — preserve for semantic edits)
- WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA (sibling re-sort fix)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Sync conflict risk:** Preventing `updatedAt` bumps may affect conflict resolution if both sides have divergent content. **Mitigation:** Preserve the existing merge semantics for content resolution; only skip the timestamp bump when the merged result equals one side.
- **Assumption:** The merge logic that compares local/remote content is sufficient to determine whether the merged result equals one side.,

data.description:
## Goal

Add a computed `currentFingerprint` field to the `wl list --json` output so that consumers (herdr selection list, TUI extension, ship gates) can determine audit freshness via the **canonical content-fingerprint gate** instead of falling back to the fragile 60-second time gate.

## Corrected context (definition gate)

The original AC ("SHA-256 hex digest of the item's description field") is **wrong**: the stored audit `fingerprint` is the audit skill's canonical composite produced by `audit_runner._compute_content_fingerprint`:

```
sha256( json.dumps({
    "path_states":      { <touched path>: {"head": <blob@HEAD|last commit>, "worktree": <status/diff>} },
    "description_hash": sha256(description),
    "key_files":        [ ...Key Files parsed from the description... ],
}, sort_keys=True) )
```

Measured against the live worklog (at the time of the fix): 27 items carry a stored fingerprint, **0** of them equal `sha256(description)`. Emitting a description-only hash would make `isAuditFresh` compare composite-vs-description and render every fingerprinted item stale. See parent WL-0MUN7QWFP0010EQC for the full analysis.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Canonical helper exists** in `packages/shared/src/audit-fingerprint.ts` — computes the audit skill's canonical composite fingerprint (per-touched-path state + description hash + Key Files) as a SHA-256 hex digest.
2. **Byte-for-byte parity** — the helper's digest equals `audit_runner._compute_content_fingerprint` for the same item and git state, including Python's `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` canonical form (`", "` / `": "` separators, `ensure_ascii` escaping).
3. **`wl list --json` includes `currentFingerprint`** for every work item in the enriched JSON output. The value is the computed canonical fingerprint when the item has a stored audit `fingerprint`; `null` otherwise (there is nothing to compare against) or when the fingerprint cannot be computed (git unavailable → fail-safe to `null`, which degrades to the time gate). Like the other audit enrichment fields (`fingerprint`, `auditedAt`, `auditResult`), it is omitted when an explicit `--fields` projection is active (the projection remains a strict subset of the requested fields).
4. **Deterministic** — the same item + git state always yields the same digest.
5. **Tests** — new tests cover the helper, the `json.dumps` canonicalisation, the JSON output field, and the freshness outcome (`isAuditFresh` flips a fingerprinted item from stale-by-time to fresh when the content is unchanged). A parity test compares the TS digest to the canonical Python digest for a fixed fixture and is skipped when the audit skill is unavailable.
6. **Human-readable output is unaffected** — non-JSON output is unchanged.

## Implementation Notes

- Hashing only: `crypto.createHash('sha256')` over a UTF-8 string; no external deps.
- Git access via an **injectable runner** (`runner(args) => {ok, stdout}`) so tests need no real repo; production passes a `child_process.execFileSync` wrapper rooted at the repo.
- Touched-file resolution: `git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=<id> --name-only --format=__WL_COMMIT__%H` + Key Files from the description. Comment-recorded commit hashes are deliberately omitted (matching the canonical `audit_runner.py check-freshness` read path); a regression test documents this.
- Path normalisation must mirror `_normalise_repo_path` (strip backticks/quotes, leading `./`).
- Compute only for items that carry a stored `fingerprint` (the primary gate requires both sides); include the field everywhere.
- No schema changes — computed at read time.

## Related

Parent: WL-0MUN7QWFP0010EQC "Audit immediately invalidated"
Canonical algorithm: `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, SorraAgents `audit_runner.py`.

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/herdr/settings.test.ts: has a 60s idle threshold by default
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
expected defaultSettings.downtimeIdleThresholdMs to be 60000 but received 75000
```

## Root Cause

The default `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` was intentionally raised from 60 s to 75 s
by WL-0MUV0VEFW007ZBB7 (`DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 75_000` in
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, consumed by `defaultSettings` in
`packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`). The assertions in
`tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` were not updated with that change, so they still
expect the stale `60000` value. The fix is to update the stale test expectations
(and the test title) to `75000` — **not** to revert the production default.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k 'tests/herdr/settings.test.ts: has a 60s idle threshold by default'` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Key Files

- `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` — stale `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` default assertions (and matching test title) to update to `75000`.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `defaultSettings` sources the value from `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — defines `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 75_000` (reference only; no change expected).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts: has a 60s idle threshold by default` passes when run against the latest `dev`, with the default `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` assertions (and the test title) reflecting the intentional `75000` default rather than the stale `60000`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (no doc change expected: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` already reflects the 75 s default from WL-0MUV0VEFW007ZBB7).
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)
- Related: WL-0MUV0VEFW007ZBB7 (parent — raised the default to 75 s)
